census.note: Reached only by code, never by data. Two of the sites are inside the neighbouring routine 0x5d4fde0 (0x5d4ff74, 0x5d4ffea); the rest span the binary.

clone_callee.arguments: rdi = out-slot pointer, rsi = source C string; returns the out-slot pointer
clone_callee.behavior: length = strlen(source); allocate length + 1 bytes with operator new[]; copy length + 1 bytes with __strncpy_chk (size argument = length + 1); store the new pointer to *out-slot; return the out-slot pointer

gates.source_string_nonnull: clone callee 0x61cf610 runs with (out slot = stack slot, source string); the returned pointer is stored to destination +0x08
gates.source_string_null: destination +0x08 is left at the zero written in the prologue; the clone callee is not called and no allocation happens

landing_pad.observed_vacuity: destination +0x08 is zeroed before the only throwing call (the clone), and is only assigned after that call returns normally, so the cleanup delete never fires on any reachable path; recorded as observed, not as a second behavior

order: destination +0x00 = source +0x00 (4 bytes); destination +0x04 = source +0x04 (2 bytes)
destination +0x08 = 0 (before any clone; this drops any prior destination string without a delete)
if source +0x08 is non-null: call clone callee 0x61cf610; destination +0x08 = cloned pointer
the post-clone delete[] check reads the stack slot after it was zeroed, so it is dead: it never frees anything on the normal path

record_layout.offset_0x00: u32 field, copied verbatim from source
record_layout.offset_0x04: u16 field, copied verbatim from source
record_layout.offset_0x06: two bytes, never read and never written by this routine
record_layout.offset_0x08: heap C-string pointer; replaced by a fresh clone of the source string, or zero when the source pointer is null

routine.arguments: rdi = destination record pointer, rsi = source record pointer, returns void
routine.note: No null check on either pointer: the first loads dereference both. The model raises on null only as a stated model guard, not as a binary claim.

transfers.note: The routine's own FDE ends at 0x5d4fd97; the bytes 0x5d4fd98..0x5d4fdd6 are the landing-pad fragment of the neighbouring routine 0x5d4fde0, not part of this routine.

unknowns: What the record denotes and what the u32/u16 fields mean; only their widths and copy order are pinned.
Whether callers always pass a fresh destination; the routine as written drops a prior destination string without freeing it, so a live destination would leak that string.
The clone callee's other callers (it is a shared string-clone helper); only its behavior as used here is pinned.
